# Preface {-}

This project is the second assignment of the ‘Data Science: Capstone’ course (PH125.9x), offered by edX HarvardX. The project aims to build and compare different Handwritten Character Recognition (HCR) models, applying different Machine Learning (ML) techniques, and using a publicly available dataset for training and validation.

# Overview and Executive Summary {#intro}

As noted in the article [Handwritten Character Recognition: A Comprehensive Survey](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10420981), Handwritten Character Recognition (HCR) plays a vital role in numerous domains, including document digitization, automatic text recognition, signature verification, and postal automation. Over the years, HCR has advanced significantly, driven by the growing demand for accurate, efficient recognition systems [@AAASM_SICI10420981].

## Project Description
::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
All the source files for *this Project* are available in the *Project*’s [GitHub repository](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own)[@edx.Capstone_CYO].
:::

In this project, we will develop and explore several HCR models, based on popular ML algorithms that convert handwritten alphanumeric symbols into a digital, machine-readable form.

We will start with [Shallow Learning (SL)](https://soulpageit.com/ai-glossary/shallow-learning-explained/) models, using [k-Nearest Neighbors (kNN)](https://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-2/ml/resampling-methods.html#sec-knn-cv-intro) and [Random Forest (RF)](https://rafalab.dfci.harvard.edu/dsbook-part-2/ml/algorithms.html#sec-random-forests) methods. These models development and evaluation are described in detail below in Sections [k-Nearest Neighbors + Principal Component Analysis (kNN+PCA) Multiclass Classifier (MCC) Model] and [Random Forest (RF) MCC Model] of *this Report*, respectively.

Next, we will try [Deep Learning (DL)](https://soulpageit.com/ai-glossary/deep-learning-explained/) models, including [Dense Neural Network (DNN)](https://smltar.com/dldnn) and, finally, [Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)](https://smltar.com/dlcnn#what-are-cnns) models, as recent research shows that DL performs better at image recognition — the task addressed by *this Project*.

A more detailed explanation of *Deep Learning* versus *Shallow Learning* can be found in the chapter [Machine Learning Methods from Shallow Learning to Deep Learning](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-69499-8_1?status=info&saved-doi=10.1007%2F978-3-031-69499-8_1) of the book [Shallow Learning vs. Deep Learning: A Practical Guide for Machine Learning Solutions](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-031-69499-8?status=info&saved-doi=10.1007%2F978-3-031-69499-8) by editors Ömer Faruk Ertuğrul, Josep M. Guerrero, and Musa Yilmaz[@Akinci2024].

The ***DNN-Based*** models are as follows:

* ***DNN-Based Basic MCC Model:*** described in Section [Dense Neural Network-Based Basic Multiclass Classifier (DNNB MCC) Model];
* ***Tuned DNN-Based MCC Model:*** described in Section [Tuned DNN-Based (TDNN) MCC Model].

The last models we will build and explore, the ***CNN-Based*** models, are as follows:

* ***CNN-Based Basic MCC Model:*** described in Section [Convolutional Neural Network-Based Basic (CNNB) MCC Model];
* ***Tuned CNN-Based MCC Model:*** described in Section [Tuned CNN-Based (TCNN) MCC Model].

Finally, we will conduct a final test of the best model we have developed, using a specially designated dataset, and see what we will achieve.

## Environment Setup
::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
The environment setup instructions are provided in the [Prerequisites & Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/README.md#prerequisites--setup) Section of the [README](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/README.md) document on [GitHub](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own).
:::

The environment setup configures an `R`-based machine learning environment with *Python* integration, required to build the *Deep Learning* models.

The installation follows a *4-step* process by sequentially running the following scripts:

* [1.install-reticulate&miniconda.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/1.install-reticulate&miniconda.R):
  1. *Installs [reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/articles/package.html):* Configures the primary `R` package, the [R Interface to Python](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/); 
  2. *Installs [Miniconda](https://continuumio-docs.readthedocs-hosted.com/miniconda/)* to manage Python virtual environments cleanly without conflicting with system Python installations. 


::: { #env_setup.step2 .sidebar}
* [2.install-tensorflow.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/2.install-tensorflow.R): 
  1. **Installs the [R TensorFlow interface](https://github.com/rstudio/tensorflow):** Loads the TensorFlow R bindings;
  2. **Configures Backend Engine:** Uses reticulate to set up a dedicated *Python virtual/conda environment* and [installs the core C++/Python TensorFlow package](https://tensorflow.rstudio.com/install/) inside it.

:::

* [3.install-keras3.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/3.install-keras3.R):
  1.  **Installs the Keras3 package:** Installs the [R Interface for Keras3](https://rstudio.r-universe.dev/keras3).
  2. **Binds High-Level Neural Network APIs:** Integrates `Keras` on top of the backend installed in [step 2](#env_setup.step2) to enable building and training *Deep Learning* models in `R`.  

* [4,install-kerastuner.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/4.install-kerastuner.R): Installs ***Hyperparameter Tuning Tools***, including [R interface to Keras Tuner](https://eagerai.github.io/kerastuneR/). Configures the [KerasTuner](https://keras.io/keras_tuner/) in `R` to automate [Hyperparameter Optimization](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/deep-learning/keras-tuner-for-hyperparameter-optimization/) (*search space*, *trial execution*, and *model evaluation*).

### Batch Execution & Cleanup Scripts

As stated in the [Prerequisites & Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/README.md#prerequisites--setup) Section of the [README](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/README.md) document on [GitHub](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own), on *Windows OS*, all 4 steps of the setup process described above can be completed automatically by launching the [__setup-env.cmd](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/__setup-env.cmd) *Windows command script* in *PowerShell* or *Command Prompt*.

The script [__uninstall-all.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/setup-env/__uninstall-all.R) cleans up the environment by wiping installed packages, *Conda environments*, and *Python bindings*.

## Running the Project

Once the system environment is fully configured, if you have enough time to execute all the scripts and automatically generate *this report* upon their completion in a single session, the easiest approach is to run the [__run-all.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/__run-all.R) script.

This script serves as a starting point for running the project execution pipeline that culminates in a *PDF report*. It coordinates the process by sequentially executing two main R scripts, ensuring the script files exist, and outputs detailed execution logs to both the console and log files.

The first script it launches, [index.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R),  is the entry point to the project's execution pipeline and the main script that runs all the other execution scripts sequentially. 

The second (and last) script it runs, [__rmd.render.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/__rmd.render.R), renders *this Report*. 

::: {.warningblock data-latex=""}
Some scripts may take a long time when executed on their first run. In particular, the longest run on the *author's laptop* (for technical specifications, see [Appendix C](#appndx_c)) was the first run of the [2.cnn-mcc.lr-tuner.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/cnn/mcc/tuner/2.cnn-mcc.lr-tuner.R) script (for fine-tuning the *CNN-based MCC* model) and took about **17 hours**.
:::

The other long-running scripts are as follows:

- For tuning and retraining the best (and *final*) *CNN-based MCC* model: 

	- [1.cnn-mcc.arch-tuner.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/cnn/mcc/tuner/1.cnn-mcc.arch-tuner.R) (took more than **6 hours** on the author's laptop);
	- [3.tcnn-mcc.final.retrain.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/cnn/mcc/tuner/3.tcnn-mcc.final.retrain.R) (took around **6.5 hours**);

- For  tuning, retraining, and evaluating the best *kNN+PCA MCC* model:

	- [3.knn+pca.best-eval.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/knn%2Bpca-mcc/3.knn%2Bpca.best-eval.R) (took more than **2 hours**);
	- [2.knn+pca.re-train.best-k.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/knn%2Bpca-mcc/2.knn%2Bpca.re-train.best-k.R) (took about **2 hours**);
	- [1.knn+pca.build&tune.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/knn%2Bpca-mcc/1.knn%2Bpca.build%26tune.R) (about *half an hour*).

- For tuning and retraining the best *Random Forest (RF) MCC* model: 
	- [2.rf-retraining.best-par.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/rf-mcc/2.rf-retraining.best-par.R) (more than **1.5 hours**).
	- [1.rf-tuning.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/models/rf-mcc/1.rf-tuning.R) (more than ***an hour***).

- For tuning the *DNN-Based MCC* model:

\newpage

- For downloading, analyzing, and preprocessing datasets:

	- [ds.kaggle.download.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/ds.kaggle.download.R) (about ***an hour***): downloads the [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters) dataset;
	- [load-raw-image-data.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/load-raw-image-data.R) (for the *Training Set*, around *40 minutes*): loads into memory the *raw image data* previously downloaded from [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters).
	- [raw-img.dat2std_bin.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/support-scripts/raw-img.dat2std_bin.R) (for the *Training Set*, about *half an hour*): prepares *standardized binary* image data;


::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
Subsequent runs of these long-running scripts will be much faster thanks to a caching mechanism that checks for the existence of the pre-computed results before running time-consuming training or evaluation code and loads the results from the cache files (if any).

Besides, any of these scripts can be launched separately, or the execution can be interrupted at any time and resumed later from the point of interruption.
:::

::: {.importantblock data-latex=""}
If the interrupted execution resumes in another *`R` Session*, the [Workspace Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L5-L160) Section (with all its subsections) of the [index.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R) script **\underline{must be run first}** at the very beginning of the *Session*. 
:::

### The Main `R` Script

The [index.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R) script serves as the main orchestrator and *entry point* for *this Project*, focused on [Multi-Class Classification (MCC)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiclass_classification) models applied to the [Kaggle Handwritten Character Image Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters) (which uses [EMNIST data](https://www.tensorflow.org/datasets/catalog/emnist) for Alphabets and Digits).
Below is a detailed description of the script's structure, workflow, and core components.

::: {.noteblock data-latex=""}
During execution, this script runs several support scripts located in the [support-scripts](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/tree/main/r/support-scripts) folder. 
[Appendix B](#appndx_b) of *this Report* describes most of them.
:::

#### Setup & Initialization

The [Workspace Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L5-L160) Section of the [index.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R) code configures and initializes the *Global Environment* for the current `R` session, as well as downloads, prepares, and preprocesses the *project’s datasets*.

::: {.importantblock data-latex=""}
Code in this Section \underline{must run at the very beginning} of every _`R` session_ **\underline{before any other script executes}**.
:::

The code in *this Section* first calls the [r-global.path.R](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r-global.path.R) script (see [Appendix B](#appndx_b.r_global.path) for details) to initialize the global variables for *this Project*’s essential `R` scripts directory paths.

Next, in the [Project Environment Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L10-L20) subsection, it executes the [setup.R](#appndx_b.setup) script, which installs the full set of required packages (those not yet installed), loads the required libraries, and completes the remaining initialization.


The remaining operations (carried out in the [Preparing Input Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L21-L160) subsection) relate to downloading and preparing the *project datasets*.

#### Downloading & Preprocessing Input Datasets

The code in the [Preparing Input Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L21-L160) subsection of the [Workspace Setup](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L5-L160) section downloads and prepares the *project datasets* in the following order:

1. In the [Download the Kaggle Dataset](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L22-L32) subsection, it runs the [ds.kaggle.download.R](#appndx_b.ds.kaggle.download) script to retrieve the [Kaggle dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters).
2. In the [Prepare Training Set](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L33-L109) subsection, the script prepares the *training datasets* by executing dedicated auxiliary scripts in the following order:
    1. In the [Training Set: Load Raw Image Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L38-L58) subsection, it runs the [load-raw-image-data.R](#appndx_b.load_raw_image_data) script to load the *raw image data* of the *Training Set*.
    2. In the [Training Set: Prepare Standardized Binary Image Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L59-L99) subsection, it runs the [raw-img.dat2std_bin.R](#appndx_b.raw_img.dat2std_bin) script to *standardize and binarize* the raw image data for the *Training Set*.
    3. In the [Prepare Training Datasets](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L100-L109) subsection, it runs the [prepare-training-set.R](#appndx_b.prepare_training_set) script to split the data of the *Training Set* and prepare *ready to use* datasets for training the *Handwritten Character Recognition (HCR)* models.
3. In the [Prepare Final Test Set](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L110-L160) subsection, the script prepares the *final test datasets* by executing dedicated auxiliary scripts in the following order:
    1. In the [Final Test Set: Load Raw Image Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L114-L132) subsection, it runs the [load-raw-image-data.R](#appndx_b.load_raw_image_data) script to load the *raw image data* of the *Validation Set*.
    2. In the [Final Test Set: Prepare Standardized Binary Image Data](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L133-L160) subsection, it runs the [raw-img.dat2std_bin.R](#appndx_b.raw_img.dat2std_bin) script to *standardize and binarize* the raw image data for the *Final Test Set*.

#### Machine Learning Model Pipelines

The [ML Models Development](https://github.com/AzKurban-edX-DS/edx.capstone.choose-your-own/blob/main/r/index.R#L161-L1066) section implements, tunes, trains, and evaluates a comprehensive benchmarking pipeline for the 39-class Handwritten Character Recognition (HCR) system.
The workflow systematically develops and tests four distinct machine learning architectures, logs evaluation metrics in a comparative results table, generates confusion matrices and per-class accuracy (PCA) visualizations, and concludes with an in-depth error analysis of common misclassifications.

## Datasets Overview

The project uses the [HandWritten_Character Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters)  downloaded from the  [Kaggle](https://www.kaggle.com) platform.

As described on the [landing web-page](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/vaibhao/handwritten-characters), the *context* of the dataset is as follows:

1. Used *EMNIST* data for Alphabets and Digits.
2. Transformed the Data using some image processing techniques and convert it to 32,32 pixel black and white images.
3. Created the Data set for special character ( @, #, $, & )
3. Merged the Categories to avoid the misclassification
4. Total 39 Categories in Train and Validation set
